page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-focused instance within the Dls_v5 series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The virtual machine provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core, the configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It features no local ephemeral disk storage, requiring external Azure remote storage volumes for persistent data. There are zero onboard GPUs. Benchmark tests demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 60731.27, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16569.0, and large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 292.88 GB/sec alongside write speeds of 135.25 GB/sec.

In multi-threaded tasks, the system delivers high throughput, registering 42665.0 in Clang software compilation and 53.15 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Single-thread processing remains average, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1671.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1900.1. Hardware-assisted cryptography tests yielded strong results, with PassMark CPU encryption measuring 58517.16. Large language model execution shows solid small-model prompt ingestion at 2137.12 tokens per second, but drops to 2.77 tokens per second during large 70B model text generation due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

The reduced memory density per vCPU provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for processing-heavy workloads that do not demand large per-core RAM allocations. Workloads matching this profile include continuous integration pipelines, software compilation, batch processing, application serving, and CPU-based cryptographic operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), and no local storage or onboard GPUs. Instruction support includes AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect top-quartile multi-core compute capability, with a PassMark CPU score of 60731.27, high software compilation rates, and strong large-block memory throughput exceeding 292 GB/sec for reads. Single-thread performance and memory caching remain in the middle tier. By constraining memory to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers cost-effective hardware utilization for compute-heavy, non-RAM-intensive tasks such as multi-threaded code builds, web serving, batch data transformation, and distributed compute clusters.
